/-!
# Conjecture 7.15

by R. Griess

Prove that if $F^*(G)$ is quasisimple and $\alpha \in \mathrm{Aut}\, G$, $|\alpha| = 2$, then
$C_G(\alpha)$ contains an involution outside $Z(F^*(G))$, except when $F^*(G)$ has quaternion
Sylow $2$-subgroups.

Here $G$ is a finite group and $F^*(G) = F(G) E(G)$ is its generalized Fitting subgroup, where
$F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup (the subgroup generated by the normal nilpotent subgroups) and
$E(G)$ is the layer (the subgroup generated by the components, i.e. the subnormal quasisimple
subgroups). A group is quasisimple if it is perfect and its central quotient is simple.
"Quaternion" Sylow $2$-subgroups are the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$, $n \geq 3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsQuasisimple (Q : Type*) [Group Q] : Prop :=
  commutator Q = ⊤ ∧ IsSimpleGroup (Q ⧸ Subgroup.center Q)
blocks.docstring:
A group $Q$ is *quasisimple* if it is perfect, $Q = [Q, Q]$, and its central quotient
$Q / Z(Q)$ is simple.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsSimpleGroup, commutator (Mathlib has no quasisimple/perfect predicate).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».IsQuasisimple
justification.why_needed: Hypothesis 'F*(G) is quasisimple' and definition of components. Defined as commutator G = ⊤ ∧ IsSimpleGroup (G ⧸ center G).

blocks.name: IsQuasisimple
blocks.text:
/-- A group $Q$ is *quasisimple* if it is perfect, $Q = [Q, Q]$, and its central quotient
$Q / Z(Q)$ is simple. -/
def IsQuasisimple (Q : Type*) [Group Q] : Prop :=
  commutator Q = ⊤ ∧ IsSimpleGroup (Q ⧸ Subgroup.center Q)

def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Subgroup G => A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal) H ⊤
blocks.docstring:
A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is *subnormal* if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$ of subgroups, each
normal in the next.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.Normal (only one step; not iterated), Relation.ReflTransGen (used as building block).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».IsSubnormal
justification.why_needed: Components are subnormal quasisimple subgroups; Mathlib has no notion of subnormal subgroup. Defined as Relation.ReflTransGen of 'A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal' from H to ⊤.

blocks.name: IsSubnormal
blocks.text:
/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is *subnormal* if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$ of subgroups, each
normal in the next. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Subgroup G => A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal) H ⊤

blocks.code:
def IsComponent (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ IsQuasisimple H
blocks.docstring: A *component* of $G$ is a subnormal quasisimple subgroup of $G$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».IsComponent
justification.why_needed: A component is a subnormal quasisimple subgroup; needed to define the layer E(G).

blocks.name: IsComponent

blocks.code:
def fittingSubgroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ Group.IsNilpotent N}
blocks.docstring:
The *Fitting subgroup* $F(G)$: the subgroup generated by all normal nilpotent subgroups
of $G$. For finite $G$ it is the largest normal nilpotent subgroup of $G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: frattini (different subgroup), Group.IsNilpotent (used as building block).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».fittingSubgroup
justification.why_needed: F(G), the join of all normal nilpotent subgroups; needed for F*(G) = F(G)E(G). Mathlib has no Fitting subgroup.

blocks.name: fittingSubgroup

blocks.code:
def layer (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {H : Subgroup G | IsComponent H}
blocks.docstring: The *layer* $E(G)$: the subgroup generated by all components of $G$.

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».layer
justification.why_needed: E(G), the join of all components; needed for F*(G).

blocks.name: layer

blocks.code:
def generalizedFittingSubgroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  fittingSubgroup G ⊔ layer G

justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».generalizedFittingSubgroup
justification.why_needed: F*(G) = F(G) ⊔ E(G), the object the problem is about.

blocks.name: generalizedFittingSubgroup

blocks.code:
def IsGeneralizedQuaternion (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k))
blocks.docstring:
A group is *generalized quaternion* if it is isomorphic to $Q_{2^n}$ for some $n \geq 3$,
i.e. to `QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k)`, of order $2^{k+2}$, for some $k \geq 1$. The case $k = 0$ is
excluded since `QuaternionGroup 1` is cyclic of order $4$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: QuaternionGroup n (Mathlib's dicyclic group, used as building block; it also covers n = 0, 1 and non-2-power n, which are not generalized quaternion).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.15».IsGeneralizedQuaternion
justification.why_needed: The exception clause 'quaternion Sylow 2-subgroups' means generalized quaternion Q_{2^n}, n ≥ 3; defined as ∃ k ≥ 1, Nonempty (P ≃* QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k)) (QuaternionGroup n has order 4n, so this is exactly Q_{2^{k+2}}).

blocks.name: IsGeneralizedQuaternion
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *generalized quaternion* if it is isomorphic to $Q_{2^n}$ for some $n \geq 3$,
i.e. to `QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k)`, of order $2^{k+2}$, for some $k \geq 1$. The case $k = 0$ is
excluded since `QuaternionGroup 1` is cyclic of order $4$. -/
def IsGeneralizedQuaternion (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k))

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.15» [Finite G]
    (hF : IsQuasisimple (generalizedFittingSubgroup G))
    (hQ : ∀ P : Sylow 2 (generalizedFittingSubgroup G), ¬ IsGeneralizedQuaternion P)
    (α : MulAut G) (hα : orderOf α = 2) :
    ∃ g : G, orderOf g = 2 ∧ α g = g ∧
      g ∉ (Subgroup.center (generalizedFittingSubgroup G)).map
        (generalizedFittingSubgroup G).subtype := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $G$ be a finite group whose generalized Fitting subgroup $F^*(G)$ is quasisimple, and
suppose that the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $F^*(G)$ are not (generalized) quaternion. Let
$\alpha \in \mathrm{Aut}\, G$ with $|\alpha| = 2$. Then $C_G(\alpha)$ contains an involution
outside $Z(F^*(G))$: there is $g \in G$ of order $2$ with $\alpha(g) = g$ and
$g \notin Z(F^*(G))$.

Here $Z(F^*(G))$ is regarded as a subgroup of $G$ via the inclusion $F^*(G) \le G$. Since the
Sylow $2$-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate, "the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $F^*(G)$ are not
generalized quaternion" is stated as: no Sylow $2$-subgroup of $F^*(G)$ is generalized quaternion.

claims.decomposer_note: Single claim for all finite groups G whose generalized Fitting subgroup F*(G) is quasisimple and every automorphism α of G of order exactly 2 (inner automorphisms allowed): some element g of G of order 2 with α(g)=g lies outside Z(F*(G)); the 'except' clause is an extra hypothesis that the Sylow 2-subgroups of F*(G) are not (generalized) quaternion, and G finite is implicit in the notebook's context.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are mathematically equivalent formalizations (finite G; F*(G) = F(G) ⊔ E(G) with F(G) the join of normal nilpotent subgroups and E(G) the join of subnormal quasisimple subgroups; quasisimple = perfect with simple central quotient; α : MulAut G with orderOf α = 2; witness g : G with orderOf g = 2, α g = g, g ∉ (center F*).map F*.subtype; exception encoded as the hypothesis that the Sylow 2-subgroups of F*(G) are not generalized quaternion, i.e. not ≅ QuaternionGroup (2^k), k ≥ 1). The final file is composed from c06 (cleanest IsSubnormal via Relation.ReflTransGen with subgroupOf-Normal, definitions, docstrings), c03/c07 (hypothesis form ∀ P : Sylow 2 F*, ¬ IsGeneralizedQuaternion P — equivalent to the ¬∀ / ¬∃ forms since Sylow subgroups of a finite group are nonempty and conjugate, but reads most directly), c01 (variable layout), plus API/test lemmas from c03/c07. Verified: QuaternionGroup (2^k) for k ≥ 1 is exactly Q_{2^(k+2)} (order ≥ 8, including Q₈, which the SL₂(q) examples show must be covered by the exception); MulAut is reducible so G ≃* G vs MulAut G is immaterial; compiles under lake --wfail with repo linters.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.15

by R. Griess

Prove that if $F^*(G)$ is quasisimple and $\alpha \in \mathrm{Aut}\, G$, $|\alpha| = 2$, then
$C_G(\alpha)$ contains an involution outside $Z(F^*(G))$, except when $F^*(G)$ has quaternion
Sylow $2$-subgroups.

Here $G$ is a finite group and $F^*(G) = F(G) E(G)$ is its generalized Fitting subgroup, where
$F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup (the subgroup generated by the normal nilpotent subgroups) and
$E(G)$ is the layer (the subgroup generated by the components, i.e. the subnormal quasisimple
subgroups). A group is quasisimple if it is perfect and its central quotient is simple.
"Quaternion" Sylow $2$-subgroups are the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$, $n \geq 3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.15»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $Q$ is *quasisimple* if it is perfect, $Q = [Q, Q]$, and its central quotient
$Q / Z(Q)$ is simple. -/
def IsQuasisimple (Q : Type*) [Group Q] : Prop :=
  commutator Q = ⊤ ∧ IsSimpleGroup (Q ⧸ Subgroup.center Q)

/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is *subnormal* if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$ of subgroups, each
normal in the next. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Subgroup G => A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal) H ⊤

/-- A *component* of $G$ is a subnormal quasisimple subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsComponent (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ IsQuasisimple H

/-- The *Fitting subgroup* $F(G)$: the subgroup generated by all normal nilpotent subgroups
of $G$. For finite $G$ it is the largest normal nilpotent subgroup of $G$. -/
def fittingSubgroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ Group.IsNilpotent N}

/-- The *layer* $E(G)$: the subgroup generated by all components of $G$. -/
def layer (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {H : Subgroup G | IsComponent H}

/-- The *generalized Fitting subgroup* $F^*(G) = F(G) E(G)$. -/
def generalizedFittingSubgroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  fittingSubgroup G ⊔ layer G

/-- A group is *generalized quaternion* if it is isomorphic to $Q_{2^n}$ for some $n \geq 3$,
i.e. to `QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k)`, of order $2^{k+2}$, for some $k \geq 1$. The case $k = 0$ is
excluded since `QuaternionGroup 1` is cyclic of order $4$. -/
def IsGeneralizedQuaternion (P : Type*) [Group P] : Prop :=
  ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ Nonempty (P ≃* QuaternionGroup (2 ^ k))

/-- A quasisimple group is nontrivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsQuasisimple.nontrivial {Q : Type*} [Group Q] (h : IsQuasisimple Q) : Nontrivial Q := by
  have := h.2.toNontrivial
  exact (QuotientGroup.mk_surjective (s := Subgroup.center Q)).nontrivial

/-- The whole group is a subnormal subgroup of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isSubnormal_top : IsSubnormal (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

/-- Every normal subgroup is subnormal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSubnormal.of_normal (H : Subgroup G) [H.Normal] : IsSubnormal H :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.single ⟨le_top, inferInstance⟩

/-- The center is contained in the Fitting subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem center_le_fittingSubgroup : Subgroup.center G ≤ fittingSubgroup G :=
  le_sSup ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

/-- The quaternion group $Q_8$ is generalized quaternion. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isGeneralizedQuaternion_quaternionGroup_two :
    IsGeneralizedQuaternion (QuaternionGroup 2) :=
  ⟨1, le_rfl, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a finite group whose generalized Fitting subgroup $F^*(G)$ is quasisimple, and
suppose that the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $F^*(G)$ are not (generalized) quaternion. Let
$\alpha \in \mathrm{Aut}\, G$ with $|\alpha| = 2$. Then $C_G(\alpha)$ contains an involution
outside $Z(F^*(G))$: there is $g \in G$ of order $2$ with $\alpha(g) = g$ and
$g \notin Z(F^*(G))$.

Here $Z(F^*(G))$ is regarded as a subgroup of $G$ via the inclusion $F^*(G) \le G$. Since the
Sylow $2$-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate, "the Sylow $2$-subgroups of $F^*(G)$ are not
generalized quaternion" is stated as: no Sylow $2$-subgroup of $F^*(G)$ is generalized quaternion.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.15» [Finite G]
    (hF : IsQuasisimple (generalizedFittingSubgroup G))
    (hQ : ∀ P : Sylow 2 (generalizedFittingSubgroup G), ¬ IsGeneralizedQuaternion P)
    (α : MulAut G) (hα : orderOf α = 2) :
    ∃ g : G, orderOf g = 2 ∧ α g = g ∧
      g ∉ (Subgroup.center (generalizedFittingSubgroup G)).map
        (generalizedFittingSubgroup G).subtype := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.15»

items: G is assumed finite ([Finite G]), as implicit in the notebook and stated in the decomposition notes; F*(G) is defined as F(G) ⊔ E(G) with F(G) the join of normal nilpotent subgroups and E(G) the join of subnormal quasisimple subgroups, which is the standard definition for finite groups.

'Quaternion Sylow 2-subgroups' is read as generalized quaternion Q_{2^n}, n ≥ 3 (including Q_8), encoded as QuaternionGroup (2^k) with k ≥ 1. This reading is forced: SL_2(7) (Sylow 2-subgroup Q_16) with an inner automorphism of order 2 violates the conclusion, so the exception must cover all generalized quaternion groups.

The exception is encoded as the hypothesis ¬ ∀ P : Sylow 2 F*(G), IsGeneralizedQuaternion P. Since Sylow 2-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate, this is equivalent to ∀ P, ¬ IsGeneralizedQuaternion P and to ¬ ∃ P, IsGeneralizedQuaternion P.
α ranges over all of MulAut G (inner automorphisms included) with orderOf α = 2 (order exactly 2, as |α| = 2 says).

An involution is an element with orderOf g = 2; C_G(α) membership is α g = g; Z(F*(G)) is (Subgroup.center F*(G)).map F*(G).subtype, i.e. the center of F*(G) regarded as a subset of G, so g need not lie in F*(G).

Definitions are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean and 1_74.lean) because the task allows only one output file; a maintainer might prefer moving the generic ones (subnormal, quasisimple, Fitting subgroup, layer, generalized quaternion) to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Two short @[category test] theorems check the bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Interpretation choices (shared by every candidate and by the decomposition note): (1) G finite, implicit in the notebook's context; (2) 'quaternion Sylow 2-subgroups' read as generalized quaternion Q_{2^n}, n ≥ 3 — this is forced, since SL₂(q) (q odd) has a unique involution and generalized quaternion Sylow 2-subgroups of every order ≥ 8, so the conclusion fails there for any α of order 2; (3) the involution is any element of G (not required to lie in F*(G)), as the text says 'C_G(α) contains an involution outside Z(F*(G))'; (4) |α| = 2 is exact order 2, inner automorphisms allowed. Bespoke definitions (quasisimple, subnormal, component, Fitting subgroup, layer, F*, generalized quaternion) are kept in the problem file as in Kourovka/1_40.lean; a maintainer may prefer moving the generic ones to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. c04 encodes generalized quaternion as QuaternionGroup n with n ≥ 2 (any dicyclic group); this is equivalent here because a Sylow 2-subgroup is a 2-group, but the 2^k form is cleaner. No candidate omitted the slot and I found no faithfulness defects in any of them; the choice among them is stylistic.
